question_text: The primary reason for introducing ceramic components in automotive engine designs is the possibility of higher operating temperatures and, therefore, improved efficiencies. A by-product of this substitution, however, is mass reduction. For the case of 1.5 kg of cast iron (density $=7.15 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ ) being replaced by an equivalent volume of PSZ (density $=5.50 \mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ ), calculate the mass reduction. Give your answer as the value of mass_reduction.The unit of the answer is kg.
response:
The cast iron occupies a volume $V = m/\rho = 1.5/7.15$. Replacing it with PSZ of the same volume gives a PSZ mass of $1.5 \times 5.50/7.15$. The mass reduction is $1.5(1 - 5.50/7.15) = 1.5 \times 1.65/7.15 \approx 0.346$ kg.

$$\boxed{0.346}$$
